revealWordProblem.title: Apply: School District Size
revealWordProblem.text: A large school district has 621,000 students in grades kindergarten through 12. The district currently has 1 teacher for every 20 students but plans to hire more teachers to have 1 teacher for every 15 students. How many teachers does the school district need to hire to reach its goal?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The district hires 10,350 teachers. It currently has 621,000 ÷ 20 = 31,050 teachers, and it needs 621,000 ÷ 15 = 41,400 teachers to reach the new ratio. The difference is 41,400 − 31,050 = 10,350 teachers to hire.

steps: 1. D - Divide: write quotient digit above the bar
4. B - Bring down: next digit from dividend
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Divide Multi-Digit Numbers is skipping a placeholder zero in the quotient when a digit doesn't divide evenly, which shifts every digit after it out of place. For example, dividing 3,216 ÷ 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1, but the next digit 2 doesn't divide by 3, so a 0 must be written before continuing — bring down the 1 to make 21 ÷ 3 = 7, then bring down 6 ÷ 3 = 2, giving the correct quotient 1,072. A student who skips writing that 0 and jumps straight to 21 ÷ 3 = 7 ends up with 172 instead of 1,072 — an answer off by a factor of ten. Always check: does a digit in your quotient go missing every time you 'can't divide'? If so, you dropped a placeholder zero.

level3.prompt: The station must load 3,360 ration packs equally into 14 storage pods. Solve it with long division. Name each step — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — and check your answer by multiplying.
level3.sentenceFrame: 3,360 ÷ 14 = ___. I divided ___ by 14 and wrote ___ , then multiplied, subtracted and brought down the next digit each time. I checked by multiplying: 14 × ___ = 3,360.
hints: Re-read the sentence frame: it wants the four named steps — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — not just the answer.
Set it up as 14 into 3,360. Since 14 does not fit into 3, your first working number is 33.
DIVIDE: 33 ÷ 14 → 2. MULTIPLY: 2 × 14 = 28. SUBTRACT: 33 − 28 = 5. BRING DOWN the 6 to make 56, then repeat — and watch what you must write when you bring down the final 0.
level3.explanation: Long division on 3,360 ÷ 14 runs the cycle three times: 33 ÷ 14 → 2 (2 × 14 = 28, leaving 5), bring down the 6 → 56 ÷ 14 → 4 (4 × 14 = 56, leaving 0), bring down the 0 → 0 ÷ 14 → 0, so a 0 must be written in the ones place. The quotient is 240 ration packs per pod, and 14 × 240 = 3,360 proves none were left over.
level3.explanationEs: La división larga de 3,360 entre 14 repite el ciclo tres veces: 33 ÷ 14 → 2 (2 × 14 = 28, quedan 5), baja el 6 → 56 ÷ 14 → 4 (4 × 14 = 56, queda 0), baja el 0 → 0 ÷ 14 → 0, así que hay que escribir un 0 en las unidades. El cociente es 240 paquetes de raciones por cápsula, y 14 × 240 = 3,360 comprueba que no sobró ninguno.
level3.promptEs: La estación debe cargar 3,360 paquetes de raciones por partes iguales en 14 cápsulas de almacenamiento. Resuélvelo con división larga. Nombra cada paso — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — y comprueba tu respuesta multiplicando.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer el modelo de oración: pide los cuatro pasos con su nombre — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — no solo la respuesta.
Escríbelo en vertical: 3,360 entre 14. Como 14 no cabe en 3, tu primer número de trabajo es 33.
DIVIDE: 33 ÷ 14 → 2. MULTIPLICA: 2 × 14 = 28. RESTA: 33 − 28 = 5. BAJA el 6 para formar 56 y repite; fíjate en lo que debes escribir al bajar el último 0.
